sections.heading: How ArionPay Works
sections.text:
ArionPay watches the blockchain and tells you when you've been paid. It never sits between your customer and your money.
1
### Customer Picks a Coin
At checkout your customer chooses a coin, such as USDT on TRON or Bitcoin. ArionPay works out the amount at the current rate and shows a QR code and an address from your own wallet. The invoice stays open for 30 minutes by default.
2
### Paid Straight to Your Wallet
The coins go from the customer's wallet to an address from your own wallet. ArionPay stores only your public key, so it can't move, hold or freeze your money.
3
### Confirmed, Then You're Told
Once the network has enough confirmations (1 on Bitcoin, 19 on TRON, for example), the invoice is marked paid. Your server gets a signed webhook, and you can get an alert by email, Telegram or Discord.

Powered by ArionPay
Your payment goes straight to the store's own wallet. ArionPay never holds your money. Refunds come from the store.
### Built for customers who pay from anywhere
Customers need no account and no browser extension. They pay from the wallet they already use.
#### Any wallet that holds the coin
Customers scan the QR code, or copy the address and amount, in any wallet that supports the chosen coin and network, such as Trust Wallet, MetaMask, Exodus, Ledger or Trezor. Paying from an exchange works too.
#### Wrong amounts are found
The amount is quoted at the current rate when the customer picks a coin, and the invoice stays open for 30 minutes by default. The exact amount is confirmed automatically, and so is a payment up to 1% off. If an amount is further off, Payment Radar finds it and you decide.
#### A signed webhook when it's paid
Once the payment has the confirmations it needs (for example 1 on Bitcoin, 19 on TRON), we send an HMAC-signed invoice.paid webhook to your server so you can deliver the order automatically. Failed deliveries are retried for about 3 days.
WHAT'S DIFFERENT

sections.heading: How ArionPay Differs from Custodial Gateways
sections.text:
Custodial gateways collect your customers' payments in their own wallets and pay you out later. ArionPay never holds your money, so there is nothing for it to hold back.
✓
### Paid Straight to Your Wallet
With a custodial gateway, payments land in the gateway's wallet and you ask for a withdrawal. With ArionPay, each payment goes straight to your own wallet.
Nothing to withdraw
✓
### We Can't Freeze Your Funds
ArionPay never has your keys, so it can't hold, freeze or move your money. Stablecoin issuers such as Tether and Circle can still freeze their own tokens on any address.
Your keys stay with you
✓
### 0.5% and No Spread
One fee of 0.5% per payment, taken from a prepaid fee balance. ArionPay adds no exchange spread, and the customer pays the network fee.
$20 fee credit to start
DASHBOARD FEATURES

sections.heading: Questions about accepting Bitcoin
sections.text:
Short answers before you take your first payment.
### How do I accept Bitcoin payments on my website?
Create an ArionPay account, connect a wallet you control, and add the checkout with a payment link, an invoice, the WooCommerce plugin or the REST API. The customer pays the exact amount shown, and the Bitcoin goes straight to your wallet.
### How much does it cost to accept Bitcoin?
0.5% of each payment, taken from a prepaid fee balance, with no monthly or setup fee. The customer pays the network fee when sending, so the Bitcoin reaches your wallet in full. New accounts start with $20 of fee credit.
### Does ArionPay hold my Bitcoin?
No. ArionPay stores only your wallet’s public key, which can show addresses but cannot move funds. Every payment arrives in your own wallet directly.
### How long does a Bitcoin payment take?
We usually see the payment within seconds of it being sent. The invoice is marked paid after 1 confirmation; the Bitcoin network makes a block about every 10 minutes on average.
### Do you support the Lightning Network?
Not today. Payments are made on the Bitcoin network itself.
### Does the price move while the customer pays?
The amount is fixed when the customer picks the coin, and it stays valid while the invoice is open.
### What if a customer pays late?
A payment up to 30 minutes late is marked paid and late. After that the invoice is closed; the customer can report the transaction ID and you decide. A late payment whose price fell in the meantime also waits for your review.
### Can I use a hardware wallet?
Yes. Connect it with its public key. We never see your private keys.

Short answers before you take your first payment.
### How do I accept USDC payments on my website?
Create an ArionPay account, connect a wallet you control, and add the checkout with a payment link, an invoice, the WooCommerce plugin or the REST API. The customer pays the exact amount shown, and the USDC goes straight to your wallet.
### How much does it cost to accept USDC?
0.5% of each payment, taken from a prepaid fee balance, with no monthly or setup fee. The customer pays the network fee when sending, so the USDC reaches your wallet in full. New accounts start with $20 of fee credit.
### Which USDC networks do you support?
Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Polygon. USDC on Solana, Base and Arbitrum is not supported today.
### Should I accept USDC or USDT?
Many merchants accept both. Each follows the US dollar, and customers tend to hold one or the other. You choose which coins each store accepts.

2 on Ethereum, 2 on BNB Smart Chain and 2 on Polygon.
### Can I see USDC in my wallet app?
Yes. Payments go to your wallet’s main address, which wallet apps such as MetaMask and Trust Wallet show.
### Is there a fee for receiving?
ArionPay charges its fee from your prepaid balance. The USDC reaches your wallet in full.

sections.heading: How Your Wallet Stays Yours
sections.text:
Custodial gateways hold your money in their wallets. ArionPay never does. Changing the wallet you're paid into also needs two-factor login, an email confirmation and a 24-hour wait.
### Your Keys, Your Coins
A new wallet's 12 secret words are made in your browser and never sent to us, and the API refuses seed phrases and private keys. ArionPay stores only your public key. If ArionPay went offline, your coins would still be in your wallet.
### Works With Wallets You Know
Use any wallet that can import 12 secret words or export an extended public key (xpub), such as Trust Wallet, Exodus, Electrum, Ledger and Trezor. ArionPay uses the public key to find your main address, the one your wallet app shows, and every payment arrives there.
### We Can't Freeze Your Funds
Your money never sits with ArionPay, so we can't hold or freeze it. Note that stablecoin issuers such as Tether and Circle can freeze their own tokens on any address.

sections.text:
Your keys are protected: showing a secret, or changing where webhooks go, needs a fresh code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password and similar), and each of these actions is recorded in your audit log and emailed to you. Do this once:
1Sign up and confirm your email

2Turn on two-factor login

3Copy the API keys

4Set the webhook URL and secret

sections.heading: Sign every request
sections.text:
Requests to your invoices are signed with your secret key. There is no Bearer token. Send these three headers, and Content-Type: application/json on POST requests:
| Header | Value
| x-api-key | Your store's public key, pk_…
| x-timestamp | The current Unix time in seconds. Requests more than 5 minutes off are rejected with 401, so keep your server clock in sync. Each signed request is accepted once: to retry, sign again with a new timestamp.
| x-signature | Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the string to sign, keyed with your secret key sk_…
String to sign
POST: <timestamp>.<raw request body>
1730000000.{"amount":"49.00","currency":"USD","test":true}
GET: <timestamp>.GET <path and query>
1730000000.GET /api/v1/invoices/6730f1c2a9e4b5d7c8f01234
The timestamp is the same string you send in x-timestamp (whole seconds, not milliseconds). For GET, sign the path and the query string exactly as they appear in the request, for example /api/v1/invoices/<id>?a=1, without the host.
- Sign the exact bytes you send. If you sign one JSON string and then let your HTTP library encode the object again (with different spacing or key order), the signature will not match.
- Send Content-Type: application/json on every POST. Without it the body is not read, and the request fails as "Invalid signature".
- Each signed request is accepted once. Two identical requests made in the same second have the same signature, so the second one is refused (401, "already used"). This also applies to two POSTs with the same body to different paths, for example the same scenario simulated on two invoices. When you retry or poll, wait until the next second and sign again.
- One exception: an exact copy of a create-invoice request that carries an idempotencyKey (in the body or as an Idempotency-Key header) is not refused. It gets the first invoice back (201), so a customer who presses your pay button twice does not see an error. Send a key with every invoice you create.

Statuses, flags and payment rules
sections.text:
| status | Meaning
| new | Created. Nothing received yet.
| pending | Enough was seen on the network; waiting for confirmations.
| paid_partial | Some money arrived, but less than the amount due. The customer can send the rest to the same address.
| paid | Paid in full and confirmed. Ship the order.
| expired | Not paid in time. Not always final: a payment that arrives within 30 minutes after expiry turns it into paid (flag late). After that the invoice is no longer watched; a payment the customer reports by its transaction ID waits for the store owner's review, as does a late one in a coin whose price has fallen since.
| cancelled | Cancelled by the store owner in the dashboard (only possible while nothing was received). No webhook is sent for it.
| claim_pending | Unpaid (new or expired), and the customer has reported a payment ("I already paid") that you have not answered yet. Nothing is confirmed on the blockchain. Do not ship.
| rejected | Unpaid (new or expired), and you rejected the customer's payment report.
| Flag | Meaning
| underpaidWithinTolerance | Paid, but a little short, within your store's tolerance (default 1%, you can set 0 to 5%).
| overpaid | Paid, and the customer sent more than the amount due.
| late | Paid after the invoice expired. Automatic within 30 minutes of expiry, which is how long an expired invoice is still watched (a store can make it shorter).
| needsReview | Needs your decision, for example a possible double payment, or a late payment in a coin whose price has fallen. reviewReason says why.
- Payments go to the wallet's main address and each invoice has a unique amount. That exact amount is confirmed automatically.
- An amount within the store's payment tolerance (1% by default, 0 to 5% per store, less or more) is confirmed automatically too, when it arrived while the invoice was open and no other unpaid invoice has a similar amount. The invoice gets the flag underpaidWithinTolerance or overpaid, and is tagged as paid with Radar.
- Any other amount is shown to the store owner by Payment Radar. If they accept it, the invoice is paid and tagged as paid with Radar.
- Older invoices with their own address follow the older rules: up to 1% short counts as paid (0 to 5% per store), paying more sets the overpaid flag, and several transactions are added up.
- An expired invoice is watched for 30 more minutes. A payment that arrives in that time counts as paid and late (a store can make this time shorter). Later the invoice is closed; a payment the customer reports by its transaction ID waits for the store owner's review. So does a late one in a coin whose price has fallen since, and one that is more than the store's tolerance above the invoice amount on an invoice with its own address.
- If an invoice is paid twice, it is marked for your review.
- An invoice is paid only after the network confirmations below. There is no zero-confirmation acceptance.
- A customer can report a payment on the checkout page ("I already paid"). Until you accept or reject it in the dashboard, an unpaid invoice shows claim_pending. Accepting it marks the invoice paid by hand (invoice.paid with manual: true).
- The customer can switch coin, or reopen an expired invoice that received nothing. Each time the invoice gets a new quote (a new address or a new unique amount) and a new price, so invoice.pending, invoice.partial or invoice.expired can be sent again for the same invoice. invoice.paid is sent once.

sections.heading: Fees and errors
sections.text:
The fee is 0.5% of each payment received, taken from your prepaid fee balance; customers' payments reach your wallet in full. There is no monthly or setup fee and no fee on test invoices. New accounts start with $20 of fee credit. When it is used up, creating a real invoice returns 402 until you top up (from $5, in crypto).
| HTTP | Meaning
| 400 | Invalid input: for example a missing amount, an amount below 0.10, an unsupported currency or coin, a malformed invoice id or invalid JSON. code no_payment_method: the store has no wallet for real invoices (or none of the requested coins can be paid to it). code unknown_asset: a misspelt coin code in allowedAssets.
| 401 | Missing or unknown key, wrong signature, no x-timestamp or one more than 5 minutes off, or a signed request that was already used (an exact copy of a create-invoice request with the same idempotencyKey is the exception: it returns the first invoice). No code field. A body sent without Content-Type: application/json is not read, so it also fails as "Invalid signature".
| 402 | code balance_empty: your fee credit is used up. Top up your fee balance (from $5, in crypto) to create real invoices again.
| 403 | code email_unverified: the account's email is not confirmed. Without a code: the store or account is disabled, or storeId does not match the key.
| 404 | No such invoice for this store (or no such path).
| 409 | code idempotency_key_reused: the key was already used with a different amount, currency or orderId. Without a code: simulating a test invoice that is already paid, or the invoice was being changed at that moment (sign again and retry).
| 429 | code rate_limited. 120 requests per minute from one IP address to each endpoint (a Retry-After header says when to try again), and 300 signed requests per minute per store in total. POST /api/v1/webhooks/test: 10 per minute.
| 500 / 503 | A problem on our side, for example a network temporarily unavailable while assigning an address (503). Retry later, signed again.

sections.heading: Already connected to the old ArionPay API?
sections.text:
Accounts and keys from the old system were not carried over: create a new account, turn on an authenticator app, connect a wallet and use the new store's keys. Shop code written for the old API, which calls https://api.arionpay.com/api/v1 and signs only the body (no x-timestamp), works when you turn on Stores > your store > Settings > "Old ArionPay (v1) integration compatibility" (it asks for an authenticator code). The old field names chain (the coin to pre-select) and returnUrl (= successUrl) are still accepted.
That switch is less safe: an old-style signature has no time limit, and webhooks are signed with your API secret. Move your code to the current scheme on this page (https://merchant.arionpay.com/api/v1, x-timestamp, ArionPay-Signature), then turn the switch off.

sections.heading: Keeping Your Account Safe
sections.text:
### What protects your account
- Two-factor login for your account.
- Protected payout-wallet changes: a new payout wallet needs two-factor login, an email confirmation and a 24-hour wait before it's used.
- Tamper-evident audit log: important actions, such as marking an invoice paid by hand, are recorded in a log that shows if it was changed.
- Alerts by email, Telegram or Discord when you're paid.
Even if someone got into your account, they couldn't move your coins: ArionPay never has your keys. See security for more.

### One fee
ArionPay charges 0.5% of each payment you receive. There is no monthly fee, no setup fee and no fee on test payments. ArionPay adds no exchange spread; the customer pays the network fee.
### The fee balance

- New accounts get $20 of fee credit, enough for about $4,000 of payments.
- When the balance is used up, new real invoices pause until you top up. Test invoices keep working.
- Top-ups start at $5 and are paid in crypto.

sections.heading: How Non-Custodial Payments Work With ArionPay
sections.text:
### Where the money goes
Custodial gateways collect payments in their own wallets and pay you out later. ArionPay works differently:
- Your wallet, your addresses: you create a wallet in your browser or connect one you already use. ArionPay stores only its extended public key (xpub), which can make addresses but can't move funds.
- Every payment matched to its order: the payment goes to your wallet's main address (the one your wallet app shows), and each invoice has its own unique amount.
- Confirmed, then paid: an invoice is marked paid once its network has enough confirmations. Today that is Bitcoin 1, Ethereum 2, BNB Smart Chain 2, Polygon 2, TRON 19, Litecoin 2, Dogecoin 20, Bitcoin Cash 6, Dash 6.
- Fee from a prepaid balance: the 0.5% fee comes out of your fee balance, so the customer's payment reaches your wallet in full. New accounts get $20 of fee credit, about $4,000 of payments.
ArionPay can't hold, freeze or move your money. Stablecoin issuers such as Tether and Circle can still freeze their own tokens on any address.

sections.heading: Selling Without a Plugin: Payment Links and Invoices
sections.text:
### Payment links
A reusable link for a product, service or donation. You set a title and description, a fixed price or pay what you want, and which coins you accept. You can let customers pick a quantity, ask for a phone number or shipping address, send them to a page of your choice after payment, pick your own link name and switch the link on or off. Each link shows its views, sales and revenue.
The customer opens the link, enters their email (and phone or address if you asked), then lands on the checkout.
### Put a link on your website
Click Get button next to a link in your dashboard. Choose a button (your text, colour, shape, size and coin logos), an image button for emails and forum posts, a text link, or a QR code to print, and copy the code or download the picture. See payment buttons.
### Invoices
A one-off request for an amount in USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, JPY or TRY, with an optional order ID, note and expiry (30 minutes by default). Each invoice has its own checkout page.
### The checkout page
A QR code, buttons that open the customer's wallet app, 9 languages, light and dark themes, and your store's logo and colour. The customer can send you an "I paid" note with the transaction ID. You can mark an invoice paid by hand (recorded in your audit log), cancel an unpaid one, and download a PDF receipt for a paid one.

sections.heading: Wrong Amounts and Late Payments
sections.text:
### The rules
Each invoice has its own exact amount, and payments go to your wallet's main address. That exact amount is how we know which invoice a payment is for.
- The exact amount: confirmed automatically.
- A little less or more: confirmed automatically if the difference is within your store's payment tolerance (1% by default, set in the store's settings, 0 switches it off). The payment must arrive while the invoice is open, and no other unpaid invoice may have a similar amount. The invoice is marked "Paid with Radar, automatic".
- Any other amount: never confirmed automatically. Payment Radar looks for the invoice it fits and shows it to you. You accept it with your authenticator code, or say it is not for this invoice.
- Late: we keep watching for 30 minutes after the invoice expires. A payment that arrives in that time is marked paid and late (you can make this time shorter in the store's settings). After it the invoice is closed. Your wallet has one address for all invoices, so an old invoice is not left waiting for money that could be mistaken for it. A customer who pays later can report the transaction ID on the payment page; you then check it and mark the invoice paid. If it was a coin whose price fell in the meantime, a late payment also waits for your review.
- Much more than the invoice: a payment that is more than your tolerance above the invoice amount is not confirmed by itself. You see what arrived and decide.
- The customer says they paid: if they give a transaction ID, it is checked on the network right away and they get a true answer.
### Chargebacks and refunds
A confirmed crypto payment can't be reversed by a card network or bank, so there are no chargebacks. If you want to refund a customer, send the coins from your own wallet. Refunds sent through ArionPay are planned.

sections.heading: Avoiding Price Swings: Stablecoins and Swaps
sections.text:
### Accept stablecoins only
If you price in dollars and want dollar-stable revenue, allow only USDT and USDC. They are available on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Polygon, and USDT also on TRON.
### Swap what you receive
If you accept Bitcoin or other coins, you can start a swap yourself from the dashboard. Swaps go through ChangeNOW and are never automatic.
### Automatic conversion
Automatic conversion of received coins (for example into USDT) is planned but not available yet.
Remember that Tether and Circle, the issuers of USDT and USDC, can freeze their own tokens on any address.

sections.heading: Test Mode: Try Everything Without Real Money
sections.text:
### How it works
A test invoice has no real address, so nobody can pay it with real crypto. Instead you pretend a payment from the dashboard or the API. An exact or late payment behaves like the real thing. A wrong amount shows what really happens: nothing is paid automatically, and in real use Payment Radar shows it to you. Your server gets the same webhooks it would in real use, marked as test. Test payments cost nothing.
You can also try a test checkout without an account.

Create a 12-word wallet in your browser, or connect Ledger, Trezor, Electrum or another wallet with its extended public key.

sections.heading: Setting Up Your Payment Wallet
sections.text:
### Two ways to add a wallet
- Create a new wallet: your browser makes 12 secret words. Write them down and keep them somewhere safe; they never leave your browser and ArionPay never sees them. You can open the same words in wallet apps such as Trust Wallet, Exodus or Electrum.
- Connect an existing wallet (advanced): paste the extended public key (xpub) from Ledger, Trezor, Electrum or another wallet. You can also restore from 12 words you already have; the public keys are worked out in your browser.
The API refuses seed phrases and private keys, so they can't end up on our servers by mistake.
### Balances and sending
Your dashboard shows the balances of your payment addresses. To send, withdraw or refund, use your own wallet app; ArionPay can't send coins for you.
### Changing the payout wallet
A change needs two-factor login, an email confirmation and a 24-hour wait, so someone who gets into your account can't quietly redirect your payments.

sections.text:
### What you need
- WordPress 6.5 or newer, PHP 7.4 or newer, and WooCommerce 8.2 or newer.
- An ArionPay store, with a wallet connected for real payments. Test mode works without a wallet.
- A shop on a public https address.
### Install
- Download the plugin.
- In WordPress open Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, choose the file, and click Install Now, then Activate.
### Connect it
- In WordPress open WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > ArionPay (crypto).
- In your ArionPay dashboard, open your store. Copy the API key (starts with pk_) into Public key and the API secret (starts with sk_) into Secret key.
- Open Webhooks in ArionPay and copy the signing secret (starts with whsec_) into Webhook secret.
- Copy the Webhook URL from the plugin settings into the Webhooks page in ArionPay.
- Turn on Enable ArionPay at checkout, save, and try it in test mode first.
### How orders update
An order is marked paid only after ArionPay confirms the payment. If a customer pays the wrong amount, the order waits, and Payment Radar shows the payment to you in your dashboard.

sections.heading: ArionPay for .NET developers
sections.text:
ArionPay on NuGet is the official ArionPay client for .NET 8 or newer. It needs nothing but .NET itself (HttpClient and System.Text.Json), keeps prices as decimal and crypto amounts as text, and checks webhook signatures on the raw body. Read more
Every call is async and takes a CancellationToken. ArionPay never holds the money: it goes straight to your own wallet.
- No dependencies: only .NET itself (HttpClient, System.Text.Json). .NET 8 or newer (8, 9, 10).
- Async all the way, with a CancellationToken on every call.
- Every invoice request carries an idempotency key, so a network error can never create two invoices.
- VerifyWebhookAsync reads the request body, checks the signature and throws ArionPaySignatureException when it does not match or is more than 5 minutes old.
- Exact amounts: prices are decimal, crypto amounts are kept as text. inv.Matches(49.90m, "USD") compares the order total to the cent.
- Thread-safe: register the client once as a singleton. You can pass your own HttpClient, for example from IHttpClientFactory.
- SimulatePaymentAsync and SendTestWebhookAsync let you test without real money.

sections.heading: Requirements and licence
sections.text:
Works with
.NET 8 or newer · ASP.NET Core minimal APIs and controllers, worker services, console apps
Cost
The library is free. ArionPay charges 0.5% per payment, with no monthly fee.
Source
Open source (MIT) on GitHub.
Setup

sections.heading: Set it up in 5 steps
sections.text:
- Step 1
### Add the package
Run dotnet add package ArionPay. It has no dependencies outside .NET.
- Step 2
### Copy your keys
In your ArionPay dashboard, open your store and copy the API key (pk_) and the API secret (sk_, it asks for your authenticator code). The webhook signing secret (whsec_) is on the Webhooks page. Keep them in environment variables or user secrets.
- Step 3
### Register the client and create an invoice
Register one ArionPayClient as a singleton. Call CreateInvoiceAsync with an InvoiceRequest (Amount, Currency, OrderId), then redirect to invoice.InvoiceUrl.
- Step 4
### Check the webhook
Set your webhook address on the Webhooks page, or per invoice with CallbackUrl. Pass request.Body and the ArionPay-Signature header to VerifyWebhookAsync, and deliver on invoice.paid.
- Step 5
### Test without real money
Create an invoice with Test = true and an Asset such as USDT_TRC20, then call SimulatePaymentAsync(inv.Id, "exact"). Your webhook gets invoice.paid, like a real payment.
After the setup

sections.heading: How a payment reaches your code
sections.text:
- invoice.pending: a payment was seen on the network and waits for confirmations. Do not deliver yet.
- invoice.paid: fully paid and confirmed, or accepted by you by hand in the dashboard. Deliver only on this event (or when GetInvoiceAsync says paid). Coming back to SuccessUrl does not prove payment.
- Before you deliver, match the invoice to your order: your OrderId or Metadata, and inv.Matches(order.Total, order.Currency).
- invoice.partial, invoice.expired and invoice.needs_review never mean deliver. A late payment can still make an expired invoice paid.
- ArionPay sends again for about 3 days when your server does not answer 2xx. Handle each ev.Id once.

sections.text:
Short answers before you add it to your code.
### Does it work with ASP.NET Core MVC controllers?
Yes. Pass Request.Body and the ArionPay-Signature header to VerifyWebhookAsync, and leave the action out of antiforgery validation: ArionPay calls it, not a browser form.
### Why does my webhook signature never match?
Do not bind the body to a model class: that is parsed and re-encoded JSON. Read the raw body, or pass bytes you already have to VerifyWebhook.
### Can I use IHttpClientFactory?
Yes. Pass your own HttpClient as the second constructor argument. It should not follow redirects.
### Which .NET versions are supported?
.NET 8 or newer: 8, 9 and 10.

The library is free and open source (MIT licence). ArionPay charges 0.5% of each payment from a prepaid fee balance, so the full amount reaches your wallet. There is no monthly or setup fee, and a new account gets $20 of fee credit.

sections.heading: ArionPay for Go developers
sections.text:
arionpay-go is the official ArionPay client for Go 1.21 or newer, with no dependencies outside the standard library. It creates and reads invoices, checks webhook signatures on the raw body, and takes a context.Context on every call. Read more
A webhook invoice and a GetInvoice result are the same arionpay.Invoice type, so one function can handle both. ArionPay never holds the money: it goes straight to your own wallet.



- No dependencies (standard library only). Go 1.21 or newer.

- Every call takes a context.Context. A cancelled context also stops the waits between retries.

- Every invoice request carries an idempotency key, so a network error can never create two invoices.

- VerifyWebhook checks the signature on the raw body and returns a *SignatureError when it does not match or is more than 5 minutes old.

- Amounts are arionpay.Amount: the text exactly as ArionPay sent it, never rounded. inv.Matches("49.90", "USD") compares the order total to the cent.

- A Client is safe to share between goroutines. The default HTTP client has a 20 s timeout and follows no redirects.

- SimulatePayment and SendTestWebhook let you test without real money.

sections.heading: ArionPay for Laravel developers
sections.text:
arionpay/arionpay-laravel builds on the official PHP library for Laravel 10 to 13 on PHP 8.1 or newer. It adds a webhook route that checks every signed update and fires it once as a normal Laravel event. Read more
In test mode every new invoice is a test invoice, so you can try the whole flow without real money. Payments go straight to your own wallet: ArionPay never holds them.
- ArionPay::createInvoice([...]) gives you the payment page address (invoiceUrl).
- Payment updates arrive as Laravel events: InvoicePaid, InvoicePending, InvoicePartial, InvoiceExpired, InvoiceNeedsReview and TestWebhookReceived.
- The route POST /arionpay/webhook checks the ArionPay-Signature over the exact body (5-minute window). Anything else gets 401 and no event fires.
- Each event fires once: it is remembered in your cache for 96 hours.
- ARIONPAY_TEST_MODE=true makes new invoices test invoices and accepts only test webhooks. A mismatch gets 409.
- php artisan arionpay:check checks your keys and shows the webhook address. php artisan arionpay:test-webhook asks ArionPay for a signed sample event.
- Every event has matches($amount, $currency), invoiceId(), orderId() and metadata() for matching the order.

sections.heading: Requirements and licence
sections.text:
Works with
Laravel 10 to 13 · PHP 8.1 or newer · built on arionpay/arionpay-php
Tested

Cost
The library is free. ArionPay charges 0.5% per payment, with no monthly fee.
Source
Open source (MIT) on GitHub.
Setup

sections.heading: Set it up in 5 steps
sections.text:
- Step 1
### Install the package
Run composer require arionpay/arionpay-laravel. Laravel picks up the service provider and the ArionPay facade by itself.
- Step 2
### Add your keys to .env
Set ARIONPAY_API_KEY (pk_), ARIONPAY_API_SECRET (sk_) and ARIONPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET (whsec_) from your ArionPay dashboard, and ARIONPAY_TEST_MODE=true. Then run php artisan arionpay:check.
- Step 3
### Create an invoice
Call ArionPay::createInvoice with the amount, orderId and an idempotencyKey such as 'order-' . $order->id, and redirect to $invoice['invoiceUrl']. The invoice sends its updates to your app's webhook route unless you pass your own callbackUrl.
- Step 4
### Deliver on InvoicePaid
Listen for ArionPay\Laravel\Events\InvoicePaid, find the order, check $event->matches($order->total, $order->currency), then deliver. If a listener throws, the route answers 500 and ArionPay delivers again later.
- Step 5
### Test, then go live
In test mode, create an invoice with 'asset' => 'USDT_TRC20' and call ArionPay::simulatePayment($invoice['id'], 'exact'), or use the Try a test payment buttons in the dashboard. Set ARIONPAY_TEST_MODE=false for real payments.
After the setup

sections.heading: How a payment reaches your code
sections.text:
- InvoicePaid: fully paid and confirmed, so deliver. It also fires for late payments, small differences inside your payment tolerance (default 1%) and payments you accept in Payment Radar.
- InvoicePending: the payment was seen on the network and waits for confirmations. Don't deliver yet.
- InvoicePartial and InvoiceExpired: not fully paid. A late payment can still follow as InvoicePaid.
- InvoiceNeedsReview: decide in your ArionPay dashboard. If you accept, InvoicePaid follows.
- TestWebhookReceived: a sample from "Send test webhook" about a made-up invoice. Never deliver for it.

sections.text:
Short answers before you add it to your code.
### Which Laravel versions does it support?
Laravel 10 to 13 with PHP 8.1 or newer. It was tested on Laravel 13.42 and 12 against a real ArionPay server.
### Do I need to write a webhook controller?
No. The package registers POST /arionpay/webhook outside the web group, so there is no session or CSRF; the signature protects it. You only listen for the events. Change the path or add middleware in config/arionpay.php.
### Why does my webhook get a 409?
Test mode and the invoice do not agree. With ARIONPAY_TEST_MODE=true the route accepts only test invoices, and with false only real ones.
### Can my listener run in a queue?
Yes. A queued listener (ShouldQueue) is retried by your queue. A listener that runs right away and throws makes the route answer 500, and ArionPay delivers again later.

The library is free and open source (MIT licence). ArionPay charges 0.5% of each payment from a prepaid fee balance, so the full amount reaches your wallet. There is no monthly or setup fee, and a new account gets $20 of fee credit.

One take on a self-hosted n8n 1.123.96 with a local ArionPay test server, in test mode: no real money. No sound; the captions are in the picture, and every step is written out below.
Before you start

sections.heading: What you need
sections.text:
- An ArionPay account: sign-up needs only an email address. Create one free.
- A self-hosted n8n that allows community nodes. Tested on n8n 1.123.96 (Node.js 22), not yet on n8n 2.x.
- Your API key, API secret and webhook signing secret, from the ArionPay dashboard.
- For real payments, your own wallet connected in the dashboard. Test invoices need no real money.
Step by step

sections.heading: Connect n8n to ArionPay in six steps
sections.text:
- 1
### Install the node
In n8n, open Settings › Community nodes and click Install. Enter n8n-nodes-arionpay, confirm the notice about community code, and install.
n8n downloads the package from npm and adds one node: ArionPay. The package has no other dependencies.
Watch this step (0:07)
your n8n
- 2
### Add your API credentials
Create a credential of the type ArionPay API and paste the API key, the API secret and the webhook signing secret from your ArionPay dashboard. Leave ArionPay Address as it is: https://merchant.arionpay.com.
When you save, n8n tests the keys with one signed request that changes nothing. In the video a wrong secret is refused first, then the right one shows "Connection tested successfully".
Watch this step (0:23)
your n8n
- 3
### Build the workflow that receives payments
Add n8n’s own Webhook node: HTTP Method POST, Respond "When Last Node Finishes", Response Data "No Response Body", and under Options add Raw Body and switch it on.
After it, add ArionPay › Webhook › Verify Webhook and pick the events you want (Invoice Paid by default). Then add your own steps: send the file, give access, or mark the order paid.
Activate the workflow and copy the Webhook node’s Production URL to the Webhooks page of your ArionPay dashboard, or send it as Callback URL with each invoice.
Watch this step (0:51)
your n8n
- 4
### Create a test invoice and pay it
In any workflow, ArionPay › Invoice › Create makes an invoice: the amount and currency, Test Invoice on, and under Additional Fields the coin, your order ID and the callback URL.
ArionPay answers with the invoice, including its payment page (invoiceUrl): that is where you send your customer. In test mode, ArionPay › Invoice › Simulate Test Payment pays it with pretend money.
Watch this step (1:15)
your n8n
- 5
### The paid webhook arrives
ArionPay signs an invoice.paid update and sends it to your workflow. Verify Webhook checks it and passes it on once, even if ArionPay delivers it again.
Your next step finds everything it needs: invoice.orderId for the order, invoice.amountFiat and invoice.currency for what was paid, invoice.paidCrypto and invoice.asset for the coin, and invoice.transactions[0].txid for the blockchain transaction. In the video, a Set node marks order ORDER-1001 as paid.
Watch this step (1:41)
your n8n
- 6
### A forged webhook is refused
Your webhook address is public, so anyone can post a made-up "invoice.paid" to it. Verify Webhook checks the HMAC signature over the exact body with your signing secret, and the time stamp.
In the video, a forged update with a wrong signature stops at Verify Webhook with "Invalid signature". The steps after it never run, and the order is not marked paid.
Watch this step (1:54)
your n8n
After the setup

sections.heading: How payment updates arrive
sections.text:
- Invoice Paid means fully paid and confirmed. That includes late payments, small differences inside your store’s payment tolerance (default 1%), and payments you accepted in Payment Radar.
- A payment that is not exact never arrives as paid until you decide in the dashboard.
- An update that fails the check (wrong signing secret, wrong or old signature) fails the workflow, so ArionPay sends it again later, for about 3 days.
- Events you did not pick end the workflow quietly with a 200 answer.
- "Send test webhook" events from the dashboard describe a made-up invoice and are skipped unless you switch them on.
- Before you deliver, check invoice.amountFiat and invoice.currency, and that invoice.test is false for real sales.
Why ArionPay

sections.heading: Questions about n8n and ArionPay
sections.text:
n8n Cloud, testing, coins and cost.
### Can I use the ArionPay node on n8n Cloud?
Not yet. n8n Cloud offers only the community nodes that n8n has verified, and we have submitted the ArionPay node for verification. Until then, use a self-hosted n8n, where any community node can be installed.
### Do I have to write code to check the webhook signature?
No. ArionPay › Webhook › Verify Webhook checks the signature, the time stamp and repeated deliveries for you. You only switch on Raw Body in the Webhook node, because the signature covers the exact bytes ArionPay sent.
### Can I try it without real money?
Yes. Switch on Test Invoice and pick a coin when you create the invoice, then use ArionPay › Invoice › Simulate Test Payment. A test invoice has no real address and costs nothing, and your workflow gets the same signed webhooks as in real use, marked as test.
### Which coins can my customers pay with?
16 coins and tokens on 9 networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin, and USDT and USDC on several networks. ArionPay › Coin lists them in n8n.
### Does ArionPay hold the money?
No. Each customer pays straight to your own wallet, and ArionPay never holds the money. It watches the blockchain and tells your workflow when the payment is confirmed.
### What does it cost?
The n8n node is free and open source. ArionPay charges 0.5% per payment, with no monthly or setup fee, and new accounts get $20 of fee credit.

sections.heading: What we still check
sections.text:
We keep fraud out without asking for your documents.
### A confirmed email
Nobody can log in before opening the confirmation link we send. Temporary and throwaway email addresses are refused.
### Strong passwords and a security check
Common and easy-to-guess passwords are refused, and sign-up and log-in pass a security check that stops bots.
### Your wallet is protected
Adding or changing the wallet your payments go to needs a code from your authenticator app, and a change waits 24 hours, with an email about it.
### A tamper-evident record
Payments and important account actions are kept in a log that shows if it was changed, and we answer lawful requests from authorities with it.
### No room for fraud
Accounts used for fraud, money laundering, sanctions evasion or other illegal activity are closed, as our Terms of Service say.
### Rules for services that hold money
If we later offer services that hold funds for you, such as managed payouts, those services may require identity checks.

sections.heading: Your own obligations
sections.text: No ID checks on our side does not mean no rules on yours. Depending on your country and your business, you may need to report crypto income, check who your customers are, or hold a licence. ArionPay does not give legal or tax advice, and it may not be used for anything illegal.

sections.heading: Questions about signing up without KYC
sections.text:
What we ask for, what we never ask for, and why.
### Does ArionPay require KYC?
No. You open an account with an email address and a password, and confirm the email. ArionPay does not ask for a passport, an ID card, a selfie, proof of address or company papers.
### Why can ArionPay work without identity checks?
Because it never holds your money. Customers pay straight from their wallet to yours, and ArionPay only watches the blockchain and tells you when a payment arrives. There is no balance of yours on our side to hold, freeze or pay out.
### What do I need to start taking payments?
An email address you can open, a password that is hard to guess, a crypto wallet of your own (or one you create in your browser with 12 secret words) and an authenticator app, which protects adding or changing the wallet your payments go to.
### Can ArionPay freeze my money?
No. Payments are in your own wallet, and ArionPay has no key that can move them. We can close an account used for fraud or other illegal activity, which stops new invoices, but the money already in your wallet stays yours. Stablecoin issuers such as Tether and Circle can freeze their own tokens on any address.
### Will you ask for ID documents later?
Not for taking payments to your own wallet. If we later offer services that hold funds for you, such as managed payouts, those services may require identity checks.
### Do I still have to follow the law?
Yes. Depending on your country and your business, you may need to report crypto income, check who your customers are or hold a licence. ArionPay does not give legal or tax advice, and it may not be used for anything illegal.

sections.text:
Adding a button, changing it later, and where the money goes.
### How do I add a crypto payment button to my website?
Create a payment link in your ArionPay dashboard, click Get button next to it, choose how it should look and copy the code. Paste it where your website lets you add HTML, such as a Custom HTML block in WordPress or an Embed HTML element in Wix.
### Do I need a plugin or any coding?
No. The button is a few lines of plain HTML that you copy and paste. There is no script to install, and it does not slow your page down.
### Where does the money go when someone pays through the button?
Straight to your own wallet. The button opens the payment page of your link, and the customer pays the exact amount shown to your wallet address. ArionPay never holds the money.
### Can I put the button in an email or a forum post?
Yes. Use the image button or a text link: they work where styled buttons are removed, such as newsletters, forum posts and GitHub pages. The dashboard gives you the HTML and the Markdown.
### Can I change the price after the button is on my website?
A payment link keeps the price it was created with. For a new price, create a new link, copy its button code into your website and turn the old link off. A link that is turned off stops taking payments, so an old button can never charge the old price.
### Can customers pay in person?
Yes. Download the link as a QR code and print it on a flyer, an invoice or a sign at your counter. Customers scan it with their phone camera and pay on the same page.

Common questions about creating and sharing payment links.
### Do I need a website or developer skills to use payment links?
No. You create the link in your ArionPay dashboard and share the URL or its QR code by chat, email or social media. The link opens a checkout page with a QR code and buttons that open the customer's wallet app.
### Where does the money go when a customer pays?
Straight to your own wallet. Every payment goes to an address of your own wallet, and ArionPay stores only your public key, so it can't move or hold your money. The sale is marked paid once the network has confirmed it, for example after 1 confirmation on Bitcoin or 19 on TRON.
### Can customers pay with different coins?
Yes. You choose which coins each link accepts, from 16 coins and tokens on 9 networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and USDC. You receive the coin the customer paid with, and you can swap it yourself from the dashboard (through ChangeNOW). Automatic conversion into a coin of your choice is planned.Coming soon
### Can I set custom amounts or take donations?
Yes. A link is either a fixed price (for example exactly $250) or pay what you want, where the customer types in the amount. You can also let customers choose a quantity, ask for a phone number or shipping address, and send them to a page of your choice after they pay.
### What do I need to sign up?
An email address and a password. Open the confirmation link we email you, and you can create links, try test payments and take real ones. No ID documents are needed.
### What are the fees for payment links?
0.5% of each payment, taken from your prepaid fee balance. Creating links is free and there is no monthly fee. New accounts get $20 of fee credit, enough for about $4,000 of payments.

Payment Radar
Customers and exchanges make mistakes. A small difference is accepted automatically, within the percentage you choose. For anything bigger, Radar finds which invoice the payment belongs to, and you decide with one click.
Start free Try a test checkout

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text:
- Step 1
### A payment arrives
A payment reaches your wallet, but no invoice has exactly that amount.
- Step 2
### Radar compares
Radar compares it with the invoices that were open at that time.
- Step 3
### Paid automatically
Within your tolerance, and only one invoice it can be for: the invoice is paid automatically.
- 4Step 4
### Or you decide
Otherwise you see "Radar found a payment" on the invoice, and you accept it or say it is not for this invoice.
Invoices paid this way are tagged "Paid with Radar", with "automatic" when no click was needed, so you can always see how they were paid.
You stay in control

sections.heading: See the payment and the reason, then decide
sections.text:
When money arrives with an amount outside your tolerance, Radar shows it on the invoice and says why it may be that customer's payment. You decide.
- Shows the amount found and the reason
- You accept it with your authenticator code
- Your shop is told only after you accept
- The invoice is tagged "Paid with Radar"
Wrong amounts guideTry a test checkout

sections.heading: What Radar looks for
sections.text:
An exchange took its fee
The payment is less by a round amount and the unique last digits of the invoice are still there. For example 25.004317 became 24.004317.
Digits were cut off
The customer rounded the amount, for example 25.004317 became 25.00.
The amount is close
The payment is within 5% of the invoice, with no clear pattern.
The customer sent a transaction ID
If a customer says they paid and gives the ID, it is checked on the network right away and they get a true answer.
The rules

sections.heading: What is automatic, and why the rest is your decision
sections.text:
### Confirmed automatically
An exact payment is always confirmed automatically. A payment within your tolerance (1% by default) is confirmed automatically too, but only when it arrived while the invoice was open and no other unpaid invoice has a similar amount. You set the percentage in the store's settings, and 0 switches it off.
### Everything else waits for you
Your wallet's address is public, and your own money arrives at the same address. A transaction ID proves nothing, because anyone can copy one from a block explorer. So when two invoices could fit, the payment is late, or the difference is bigger, Radar shows it and you decide.
### Late payments
An exact payment that arrives up to 30 minutes after the invoice expired is marked paid and late. After that the invoice is closed, so old invoices are not left waiting for money that could be mistaken for them. A customer who pays later can report the transaction ID, and you decide.

sections.heading: ArionPay for Blesta
sections.text:
ArionPay for Blesta is a non-merchant gateway for Blesta 5. The client presses Pay with crypto, pays on the ArionPay page, and the money goes straight to your own wallet: ArionPay never holds it. Read more
When ArionPay confirms the full payment, Blesta records one approved transaction and applies it to the invoices it was for. Version 1.0.0 has not yet been tried on a licensed Blesta install, so please start in Test mode.
- One payment is one approved transaction, applied to the invoices it was for.
- Repeated updates for the same payment change that one transaction, so money is never added twice.
- The transaction id is arionpay- plus the ArionPay invoice id.
- Both secrets are stored encrypted by Blesta.
- A test invoice is never accepted while Test mode is off, and a real one is never accepted while it is on.
- Details of every update are in Tools > Logs > Gateway, without keys or secrets.

sections.heading: How invoices change
sections.text:
- The client presses Pay with crypto and goes to the ArionPay page. Pressing it again opens the same page while it is still open.
- When ArionPay confirms the full payment, Blesta records one approved transaction for the amount paid and applies it to the invoices it was for.
- "Payment seen", partial, expired and "needs review" updates only go to the gateway log. They do not create a pending transaction.
- A payment that is not exact goes to Payment Radar. A small difference inside your store's payment tolerance (default 1%) is accepted automatically; anything else you decide.
- If the invoice total changes after the client went to pay, the next press makes a new ArionPay invoice for the new total.
- Coming back from the payment page records nothing. Only ArionPay's signed update approves a payment.

sections.heading: Questions about ArionPay for Blesta
sections.text:
Short answers before you install it.
### Is the ArionPay Blesta gateway ready for live payments?
It is a pre-release, published for testing. It has been checked against a stand-in of Blesta, but not yet tried on a licensed Blesta install. Please start in Test mode.
### Does it support automatic recurring charges?
No. Automatic recurring charges are not possible with crypto, so clients pay each invoice by hand.
### What happens if a client pays an invoice that changed?
If the invoice total changes, the next press makes a new ArionPay invoice for the new total. If the old one gets paid anyway, Blesta records what was really paid and shows the rest as still due.
### How do I refund a crypto payment in Blesta?
Send the refund from your own wallet, then record it in Blesta by hand.
### What does ArionPay for Blesta cost?
The Blesta payment gateway is free and open source (MIT licence). ArionPay charges 0.5% of each payment from a prepaid fee balance, so the full amount reaches your wallet. There is no monthly or setup fee, and a new account gets $20 of fee credit.

The ArionPay Discord shop bot is one Node.js file with no Discord library, run on your own server with a public https address. Members use /shop or /buy, press a button and pay on the ArionPay page; everything they see is private to them. Read more
When ArionPay confirms the payment, the bot gives the role, sends the item by direct message and, if you want, posts the sale in a channel for you and your moderators. Open orders are also re-checked every 300 seconds by default, so a missed payment update still gets delivered.
- /shop and /buy commands, with replies only the member sees.
- Each item gives a role, sends a text, or both.
- An optional sale notice in a channel for you and your moderators.
- If a member does not accept DMs, the item is shown in their private pay message during the first 15 minutes.
- Each order is delivered once, and a doubled button press never makes a second invoice.
- Discord’s request signatures and ArionPay’s webhook signatures are both checked.
- A test invoice never delivers in live mode, and a live one never in test mode.

Discord only lets a bot give roles below its own. In Server Settings > Roles, drag the bot’s role above the roles it sells, and give the bot Manage Roles.

When the payment is confirmed, the amount is added to the client's balance and the invoice is paid from it, the same way FOSSBilling's other gateways work. It was tested on a real FOSSBilling 0.8.9 install.

medusa-payment-arionpay is a Medusa 2 payment provider for crypto. Your storefront sends the customer to the ArionPay page, and the money is paid straight to your own wallet: ArionPay never holds it. Read more
When ArionPay confirms the full payment, its signed webhook makes Medusa authorize the payment session and turn the cart into an order, even if the customer never comes back. It is a package for developers who run their own Medusa backend and storefront.
- Published on npm as medusa-payment-arionpay, with no dependencies besides Medusa itself.
- A signed invoice.paid webhook turns the cart into an order, even if the customer never comes back.
- When the storefront completes the cart, the provider asks ArionPay directly, so a lost webhook is caught.
- A session counts as paid only when ArionPay itself confirms the invoice for the same amount, currency and mode.
- If the cart changes, the next session gets a new invoice for the new total.
- Crypto payments are final, so the payment is captured at once.
- testMode is on unless you set it to false, so a missing setting never takes real money.

sections.heading: ArionPay for n8n
sections.text:
n8n-nodes-arionpay adds one node, ArionPay, to n8n. It creates and reads invoices, simulates test payments, lists coins and rates, and checks the payment updates that n8n’s own Webhook node receives. Read more
Verify Webhook checks the signature over the exact body and passes on only the events you pick, such as Invoice Paid, once each. After it come your own steps: send the file, give access, or mark the order paid in your sheet.
- Invoice: create an invoice and get its payment page address, read an invoice, or simulate a test payment.
- Verify Webhook checks the signature over the exact body, with a 5-minute clock window.
- Each event is passed on once, even when ArionPay delivers it again. An active workflow remembers the last 300 event ids.
- Pick the events you want, and let a workflow take only test or only live invoices.
- Coin and Rate: list the coins ArionPay takes, and coin prices.
- The ArionPay API credentials also sign requests made with n8n’s HTTP Request node.
- No other packages: requests are signed with Node’s own crypto.

sections.heading: How payment updates arrive
sections.text:
- Invoice Paid means fully paid and confirmed. That includes late payments, small differences inside your store’s payment tolerance (default 1%), and payments you accepted in Payment Radar.
- A payment that is not exact never arrives as paid until you decide in the dashboard.
- An update that fails the check (wrong signing secret, wrong or old signature) fails the workflow, so ArionPay sends it again later, for about 3 days.
- Events you did not pick end the workflow quietly with a 200 answer.
- "Send test webhook" events from the dashboard describe a made-up invoice and are skipped unless you switch them on.
- Before you deliver, check invoice.amountFiat and invoice.currency, and that invoice.test is false for real sales.

sections.heading: Questions about ArionPay for n8n
sections.text:
Short answers before you install it.
### Is there an ArionPay Trigger node in n8n?
Not since version 2.0.0, which removed it so the package can be verified by n8n. Payment updates come in through n8n’s own Webhook node, followed by ArionPay > Verify Webhook. The output fields are the same.
### Why switch on Raw Body in the Webhook node?
The signature covers the exact bytes ArionPay sent. Without Raw Body, Verify Webhook stops with a message that says to switch it on.
### Can I test the workflow without real money?
Yes. Tick Test Invoice and fill Coin when you create the invoice, then use ArionPay > Invoice > Simulate Test Payment, or the Try a test payment buttons in the dashboard.
### How fast must the workflow answer?
ArionPay waits 10 seconds for the answer. Keep the steps after Verify Webhook short, or ArionPay sends the update again and Verify Webhook skips it as a repeat.
### What does ArionPay for n8n cost?
The n8n community node is free and open source (MIT licence). ArionPay charges 0.5% of each payment from a prepaid fee balance, so the full amount reaches your wallet. There is no monthly or setup fee, and a new account gets $20 of fee credit.

sections.heading: Questions about ArionPay for Paymenter
sections.text:
Short answers before you install it.
### Which Paymenter versions does the ArionPay gateway work with?
Paymenter 1.x. It was tested on a real Paymenter 1.5.9 with PHP 8.3 and MariaDB.
### Why do I have to save the gateway twice?
Paymenter encrypts the secret fields only when a gateway is saved from its edit page. After you create the gateway, open it again and press Save once more.
### Does it support automatic renewals?
No. Billing agreements are not supported, because crypto payments are one-off. Renewal invoices are paid like any other invoice.
### What if a client pays an invoice that is already paid?
The second payment is not added. A failed transaction and a log warning ask you to check your wallet and refund the client.
### What does ArionPay for Paymenter cost?
The Paymenter gateway extension is free and open source (MIT licence). ArionPay charges 0.5% of each payment from a prepaid fee balance, so the full amount reaches your wallet. There is no monthly or setup fee, and a new account gets $20 of fee credit.

sections.heading: ArionPay for Telegram
sections.text:
The ArionPay Telegram shop bot is one Node.js file that you run on your own server or computer. Customers send /start, tap an item and pay on the ArionPay page; when ArionPay confirms the payment, the bot sends what you wrote for that item in products.json. Read more
With a public https address it gets signed webhooks at once, and without one it asks ArionPay about open orders every 30 seconds. No database or framework is needed.
- Products live in one products.json file: name, price, currency and what the bot sends after payment.
- Each order is delivered once.
- Runs anywhere: signed webhooks with a public https address, or a check of open orders every 30 seconds without one.
- An item is sent only when ArionPay confirms the full payment for that order, in the same currency and amount.
- A test invoice never delivers in live mode, and a live one never in test mode.
- Orders are kept in orders.json next to the bot.
- One file, Node.js 18 or newer, no database or framework.

No, leave it off for this gateway. The module always charges in the WHMCS invoice's own currency.

You send the refund from your own wallet. The module does not send refunds.

sections.heading: ArionPay compared with custodial gateways and card processors
sections.text:
A general comparison by type of provider. Every provider is different, so check the terms of any service you are considering.
### Non-custodial
Custodial gateways receive your money into their own wallets and pay you out later. With ArionPay, customers pay straight to your own wallet. We store only your public key, which cannot move funds.
We cannot freeze or hold your funds
### Test before you go live
Create test invoices and simulate exact, wrong and late payments. You sign up with an email address and confirm it before your first login.
No fee on test payments
### 0.5% per payment, $20 to start
No monthly or setup fee. The fee comes from a prepaid balance, so customer payments reach your wallet in full. New accounts get $20 of fee credit, about $4,000 of payments.
No monthly fee
### Paid after real confirmations
We see a payment within seconds and mark the invoice paid once the network confirms it: 1 confirmation on Bitcoin, 2 on Ethereum, 19 on TRON. Then your server gets a signed webhook.
No chargebacks

Security
ArionPay is built so that even a full break-in on our servers cannot move your money. This page explains how, and where the limits are.

How it works

sections.heading: Seven layers, none of which needs your keys
sections.text:
-
### Watch-only by design
- When you create a wallet, the 12 secret words are made in your browser and never sent to us.
- We receive only extended public keys. They can create receiving addresses and read balances, but cannot sign a transaction.
- The server refuses any request that contains a seed phrase or a private key.
-
### Every payment matched to exactly one invoice
- Payments go to your wallet's main address, the one your wallet app shows (Trust Wallet, MetaMask, Exodus…), and each invoice has its own unique amount. No two open invoices share an amount, and each transfer is counted for one invoice only.
- Payments that reached the address before the invoice was shown never count for it.
- The exact amount is matched automatically. An amount within your tolerance (1% by default, 0 to switch it off) is matched only if it arrived while the invoice was open and no other unpaid invoice has a similar amount. Everything else waits for your decision, so an old, late or unclear payment is never credited to another customer.
-
### Protected payout-wallet changes
- Adding your first wallet needs a code from your authenticator app; it works straight away.
- Adding or changing a wallet later also needs a confirmation link sent to your email.
- The new wallet becomes active only 24 hours after you confirm, and you can cancel the change until then.
-
### Account protection
- Two-factor login with an authenticator app. Each code works once.
- Changing a wallet, showing the API secret, changing webhooks or where Telegram and Discord alerts are sent, or marking an invoice paid needs a fresh code from your authenticator app, and always sends you a security email.
- Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes.
-
### Tamper-evident audit log
- Every payment, address, webhook and account action is written to an append-only log.
- Each entry is chained to the one before it, and a signed summary of each day is stored outside the database.
- Any later change to the log shows up when it is verified, including changes made by an administrator.
-
### Data and backups
- Personal data such as customer email and IP addresses is stored encrypted, with the keys kept apart from the data.
- Backups are encrypted with a key that is kept offline, and restores are tested.
- Personal data is anonymised after its retention period ends; payment records stay, without the personal details.
-
### Signed API and webhooks
- API requests are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over a timestamp and the body; requests older than 5 minutes are refused.
- Webhooks are signed the same way with a separate secret, so your server can check where they came from.

sections.heading: Questions about swaps
sections.text:
How swaps work today, and what is coming.
### Does ArionPay hold my coins during a swap?
No. You send the coins from your own wallet to the deposit address ChangeNOW gives you, and ChangeNOW sends the new coins to a fresh address in your own wallet. ArionPay shows you the quote and keeps track of the swap; it never holds the coins.
### Who sets the rate?
ChangeNOW. The amount you see before you confirm is an estimate, not a fixed or guaranteed price. What you receive can be different if the market moves before your coins arrive.
### Which coins can I swap?
BTC, ETH, BNB, TRX, LTC, DOGE, BCH and DASH; USDT on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, TRON and Polygon; and USDC on Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain. POL and USDC on Polygon cannot be swapped yet.
### What does a swap cost?
ChangeNOW’s own fees are included in its rate. ArionPay adds a service fee, shown before you confirm, which is taken from your prepaid fee balance only when the swap finishes.
### Can every payment be converted automatically?
Not yet. Automatic conversion of every payment into an asset you choose, for example USDT, is coming soon. Today, you start each swap yourself from the dashboard.

sections.heading: Works today: send a checkout link from your own bot
sections.text:
Your bot creates an invoice with one signed API request and sends the customer the invoice_url as a button. The customer pays on the ArionPay checkout page, straight to your wallet.

Copy code
```
import hashlib, hmac, json, os, time
import requests
import telebot  # pip install pyTelegramBotAPI requests

bot = telebot.TeleBot(os.environ["TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"])

API_KEY = os.environ["ARIONPAY_API_KEY"]        # pk_...
API_SECRET = os.environ["ARIONPAY_API_SECRET"]  # your store's secret
BASE_URL = os.environ["ARIONPAY_URL"]           # your ArionPay address

def create_invoice(payload):
    body = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"))
    ts = str(int(time.time()))
    sig = hmac.new(API_SECRET.encode(), f"{ts}.{body}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    res = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/api/v1/invoices",
        data=body,  # send exactly the bytes you signed
        headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "x-api-key": API_KEY,
            "x-timestamp": ts,
            "x-signature": sig,
        },
        timeout=15,
    )
    res.raise_for_status()
    return res.json()

@bot.message_handler(commands=["buy"])
def buy(message):
    user_id = message.from_user.id
    invoice = create_invoice({
        "amount": "29.99",
        "currency": "USD",
        "orderId": f"tg-{user_id}-{int(time.time())}",
        "metadata": {"telegramUserId": user_id},
    })
    markup = telebot.types.InlineKeyboardMarkup()
    markup.add(telebot.types.InlineKeyboardButton("Pay with crypto", url=invoice["invoice_url"]))
    bot.send_message(message.chat.id, "Your order: $29.99. Tap below to pay.", reply_markup=markup)

# (check the ArionPay-Signature header first; see /docs).

bot.infinity_polling()

sections.heading: Questions about the white-label API
sections.text:
How the payment stays on your own site, what it costs, and what is coming.
### Do my customers leave my website?
No. Your own page shows the exact amount, the address and a QR code, and the customer pays from their wallet. If you like, add a link to the ArionPay payment page for customers who need help.
### Does ArionPay hold the money?
No. The address is your own wallet’s address, so the payment goes straight to you. ArionPay watches the blockchain, matches the payment to its invoice and tells your server when it is paid.
### Which coins can I offer?
Every coin your store accepts. The codes are listed at GET /api/v1/currencies, for example USDT_TRC20, USDC_POLYGON or BTC. An invoice is for one coin, so let the customer choose first and then create the invoice with that coin.
### How does my website know the invoice is paid?
Your server gets a signed invoice.paid webhook when the network has confirmed the payment. While the customer waits, your server can also ask GET /api/v1/invoices/:id for the status and the confirmations.
### What if a customer sends the wrong amount?
The same rules as on the ArionPay checkout: the exact amount, and a small difference within your tolerance when only one invoice fits, are confirmed automatically. Payment Radar finds any other amount and shows it in your dashboard for you to decide.
### Does it cost more?
No. It is the same 0.5% per payment as the ArionPay checkout, with no monthly fee.
### Can the ArionPay checkout page run on my own domain?
Not yet: that is on our Roadmap. Today the ArionPay checkout can show your store’s logo and brand colour, and the white-label API lets you build the whole payment page yourself.

sections.heading: Facts
sections.text:
- Fee: 0.5% of each payment received, taken from a prepaid fee balance. No monthly fee, no setup fee, no fee on test payments. New accounts get $20 of fee credit.
- Supported (16 coins and tokens on 9 networks): Bitcoin (BTC); Ethereum (ETH, USDT, USDC); BNB Smart Chain (BNB, USDT, USDC); Polygon (POL, USDT, USDC); TRON (TRX, USDT); Litecoin (LTC); Dogecoin (DOGE); Bitcoin Cash (BCH); Dash (DASH).
- Not supported: Solana, TON, Base, Arbitrum, XRP, Cardano, DAI.
- Wallets: the merchant's own. ArionPay stores only extended public keys (xpub/zpub); seed phrases and private keys are refused by the API. Every network: payments go to the wallet's main address (the one wallet apps show) and each invoice has a unique amount (the last digits identify the payment).
- Payment rules: the exact amount of an invoice is confirmed automatically. So is a payment within the store's tolerance (1% by default, up to 5%; 0 switches it off) when it arrived while the invoice was open and can only belong to one invoice. Payment Radar finds any other amount and shows it to the merchant, who decides. An exact payment that arrives up to 30 minutes after the invoice expired is marked paid and late; after that the invoice is closed, and the customer can report the transaction ID for the merchant to check.
- Invoices expire after 30 minutes by default (5-1440 minutes configurable).
- Test mode: test invoices never get a real address; payments are simulated; webhooks carry "livemode": false.
- Sign-up: an email address; real payments after the email is confirmed. No identity documents.
- Integrations today: REST API and webhooks, payment links and buttons, dashboard invoices, plugins for 24 platforms (WooCommerce, Magento 2, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Shopware 6, Drupal Commerce, VirtueMart, HikaShop, Easy Digital Downloads, Odoo, Medusa, WHMCS (pre-release), Blesta (pre-release), FOSSBilling, Paymenter, WordPress payment buttons, Paid Memberships Pro, LifterLMS, Tutor LMS, GiveWP, Charitable, n8n, Telegram, Discord), and official libraries for Node.js, Python, PHP, Laravel, Go, Ruby, Java, .NET. Each has its own page, listed under Pages.
- White-label API: POST /api/v1/invoices with "asset" (e.g. USDT_TRC20) returns data.address and data.amount_crypto at once, so a shop can show the payment on its own page (no redirect); follow it with GET /api/v1/invoices/:id and the invoice.paid webhook. The ArionPay checkout on the merchant's own domain is not available yet (Roadmap).
- Payment buttons: in the dashboard, Payment links → Get button turns a link into an HTML button (text, colour, shape, size, coin logos), an image button (HTML or Markdown), a text link or a QR code (PNG/SVG). Plain HTML, no script.
- Coming soon (not available yet): automatic conversion of received coins, mass payouts and managed payout wallets, a Shopify app, Telegram Mini App checkout, the ArionPay checkout on the merchant's own domain, fiat settlement, more networks.

sections.heading: API (summary)
sections.text:
Base URL: `https://merchant.arionpay.com` (the dashboard, checkout pages and API live there; the website is arionpay.com). Authentication is HMAC with the store's public key and secret.

Machine-readable API description: [OpenAPI 3](https://arionpay.com/openapi.json) and a [Postman collection](https://arionpay.com/arionpay-api.postman_collection.json) (requests signed by its pre-request script).

- Headers: `x-api-key: pk_...`, `x-timestamp: <unix seconds>`, `x-signature: <hex>`
- POST signature: `hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>"))`
- GET signature: `hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.GET <path and query>"))`
- Requests older than 5 minutes are rejected.

Endpoints:

- `POST /api/v1/invoices` - create an invoice. Body: `amount` (required), `currency` (default "USD"), `orderId`, `customerEmail`, `description`, `successUrl`, `cancelUrl`, `expiresMin`, `metadata`, `idempotencyKey`, `allowedAssets`, `test`. Returns 201 `{ "status": "success", "id", "invoice_url", "data": { "id", "invoice_url", "amount_fiat", "currency", "status", "asset", "address", "amount_crypto", "expires_at", "order_id" } }`. Send the customer to `invoice_url`.
- `GET /api/v1/invoices/:id` - read an invoice.
- `GET /api/v1/invoices?status=&since=&until=&before=&orderId=&test=&limit=` - this store's invoices, newest first (summary only; `nextBefore` for the next page).
- `POST /api/v1/invoices/:id/simulate` - test invoices only. Body `{ "scenario": "detected" | "confirm" | "exact" | "underpaid_1pct" | "underpaid_5pct" | "overpaid" | "partial_half" | "late" }`.

Invoice statuses: `new`, `pending` (seen, confirming), `paid_partial`, `paid`, `expired`, `cancelled`. Flags: `overpaid`, `underpaidWithinTolerance`, `late`, `needsReview`.

Webhooks: `POST` to the merchant's https URL. Body `{ "id": "evt_...", "type": "invoice.paid", "created": <unix>, "livemode": true, "data": { "invoice": { ... } } }`. Headers `ArionPay-Event`, `ArionPay-Event-Id`, `ArionPay-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC_SHA256(webhookSecret, "<t>.<raw body>")>`. Events: `invoice.pending`, `invoice.partial`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.expired`, `invoice.needs_review`. Failed deliveries are retried for about 3 days. The webhook secret is separate from the API secret.

Frequently asked questions
sections.text:
- Does ArionPay hold my money? No. Customers pay straight to addresses from the merchant's wallet. ArionPay stores only the public key, which cannot move funds.
- What if a customer sends the wrong amount? Only the exact amount is confirmed automatically. Payment Radar finds other amounts and the merchant decides.
- What if they pay after the invoice expires? The address is watched for 7 more days. A late payment is marked paid and late; if the coin's price fell, it waits for the merchant's review.
- Which wallets work? Any wallet that imports 12 words or exports an extended public key, for example Trust Wallet, Exodus, Electrum, Ledger and Trezor.
- How are fees charged? 0.5% of each payment from a prepaid fee balance. New accounts start with $20 of credit. When the credit is used up, new real invoices pause until the merchant tops up (from $5, paid in crypto).
- Can I test without real money? Yes, with test invoices and simulated payments.
- How is a merchant notified? Dashboard, email, Telegram, Discord, and signed webhooks.
- What is needed to sign up? An email address. Real payments start after the email is confirmed.

info.title: ArionPay API
info.description: Signed requests send x-api-key (store public key pk_...), x-timestamp (Unix seconds) and x-signature = hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret key, "<timestamp>.<raw body>")) for POST, or "<timestamp>.GET <path and query>" for GET, and Content-Type: application/json on POST. Requests more than 5 minutes off are rejected with 401. Each signed request is accepted once: two identical requests in the same second have the same signature, so wait for the next second before you retry or poll. The exception is an exact copy of POST /api/v1/invoices with the same idempotencyKey (or Idempotency-Key header): it returns the first invoice (201). Webhooks (ArionPay-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC_SHA256(webhook secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>) are described at https://arionpay.com/docs#webhooks.

callbackUrl.description: https, port 443 or 8443, public IP address

metadata.description: Up to 4 KB, 4 levels; keys may not start with $ or contain a dot

storeId.description: Optional; must be the key's store

get.summary: List this store's invoices, newest first
get.description: A short summary per invoice (no customer email, metadata or addresses). For the next page pass nextBefore as before. Sign the exact path and query you send; add nonce (any value) to repeat the same request within one second.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Created before (nextBefore of the previous page)

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: Ignored by the server; makes a repeated signed GET unique
